hints: Focus on what LiAlH4 actually does, it reduces carbonyl compounds to alcohols, so first work out what alcohol each starting material would give.
Recall that two optical isomers means a racemic pair of enantiomers, so the alcohol product must contain a chiral carbon with four different groups.
Draw the reduced product for the unsymmetrical ketone and check its middle carbon, then compare it with the symmetrical ketone and the primary alcohol products.
walkthrough:
**Recall LiAlH4 reduction products**

Think of LiAlH4 as a source of hydride that adds H across the C=O bond. Aldehydes give primary alcohols, ketones give secondary alcohols, and carboxylic acids give primary alcohols.

$$\text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}, \quad \text{RCOR'} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)R'}, \quad \text{RCO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Condition for two optical isomers**

Two optical isomers means a pair of enantiomers formed in equal amounts. That happens when the product has exactly one chiral centre, a carbon bonded to four different groups.

$$\text{chiral centre = C bonded to H, OH, and two different alkyl groups}$$

**Apply to the four compounds**

Option A, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$ (butan-2-one), gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ (butan-2-ol). The C-OH carbon is bonded to H, OH, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so it is chiral.

Reduction creates a planar C=O attacked equally from both sides, so both enantiomers form as a racemic mixture. This matches the question.

options.A: Butan-2-one is reduced to butan-2-ol, CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3. The carbon bearing OH is attached to H, OH, CH3 and CH2CH3, four different groups, so it is chiral. Attack from either face of the planar carbonyl gives a racemic pair, two optical isomers.
options.B: Butanal, CH3CH2CH2CHO, is an aldehyde and gives the primary alcohol butan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2CH2OH. The CH2OH carbon has two H atoms, so it cannot be chiral and no optical isomers form.
options.C: Pentan-3-one, CH3CH2COCH2CH3, gives pentan-3-ol, CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3. The C-OH carbon is bonded to H, OH and two identical ethyl groups, so it is achiral. Students who forget to check that the two sides are identical often pick this trap.
options.D: 3-methylbutanoic acid, CH3CH(CH3)CH2CO2H, gives the primary alcohol 3-methylbutan-1-ol, (CH3)2CHCH2CH2OH. No carbon has four different groups, the branched carbon has two identical methyl groups, so the product is achiral.
